results.title: Falsification Tests | Erin Hartman
results.content: Falsification tests are statistical tests that researchers conduct to marshal evidence that their design is valid their conclusions are sound. Current practice in falsification testing does not allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their assumptions are warranted. By failing to detect a problem with the design assumptions, rather than providing evidence of a valid design, researchers conflate statistical insignificance with substantive homogeneity. Statistical tests of equivalence are a natural way to conduct a falsification test, and allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their research design is sound and their conclusions are warranted. I have extended this work to the regression discontinuity setting in Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs. ### Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Recent emphasis on credible causal designs has led to the expectation that scholars justify their research designs by testing the plausibility of their causal identification assumptions, often through balance and placebo tests.

results.title: Falsification Tests | Erin Hartman
results.content: Falsification tests are statistical tests that researchers conduct to marshal evidence that their design is valid their conclusions are sound. Current practice in falsification testing does not allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their assumptions are warranted. Daniel Hidalgo), argues that falsification tests should be structured so that the responsibility lies with researchers to positively demonstrate that the data is consistent with their identification assumptions or theory. This means that researchers should begin with the initial hypothesis that the data is *inconsistent* with a valid research design, and only reject this hypothesis if they provide sufficient statistical evidence in favor of data consistent with a valid design. Statistical tests of equivalence are a natural way to conduct a falsification test, and allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their research design is sound and their conclusions are warranted. I have extended this work to the regression discontinuity setting in Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs.

results.title: Placebo test: Significance and symbolism
results.content: Placebo tests are used to validate carbon trading policy results and reduce the influence of random factors. These tests ensure that observed effects stem from the policy itself, not from other policies or random occurrences. The Placebo test, according to the text, validates research results by confirming policy effects aren't due to random factors, omitted variables, or other policies. (2) A placebo test is conducted to verify the robustness of research results by simulating an ineffective intervention, ensuring that the observed effects are not due to unobserved factors or random chance. (3) A placebo test involves artificially altering a key parameter, like the boundary, to confirm that the observed effects are due to the actual policy and not random chance. (1) A test where the policy intervention is applied fictitiously to ensure that the observed effects are due to the actual policy and not other factors.

results.title: Placebo Book Chapter 1 - Placebo History and Terminology - Zeebo® USA
results.content: In 1978 a landmark experiment showed how pain relief from placebo actually has a physical effect on our body. Levine’s experiment showed that naloxone not only prevented pain relief from opioids, but it also blocked pain relief from placebo. Recent studies using the brain-imaging technology showed that taking placebos leads to neurobiological patterns in the brain that can also be observed when powerful pain relievers are given. Petrovic **et al** *(2002),* *demonstrated that the same regions of the brain are activated when patients receive an opioid pain reliever (remifentanil) or when patients take a placebo. Similar brain imaging studies by Zubieta et al* *(2005)* *and Eippert et al* *(2009) also showed that placebos trigger brain responses that ameliorate pain.*. FDA reviewed clinical trials are usually randomized, double blind studies, neither doctor nor patient know if the drug or the placebo are administered. Taking placebos in an honest way made a meaningful clinical difference for these patients.
